content: The transfer of knowledge will be utilized to convene relevant stakeholders to identify and evaluate the priorities, barriers, and facilitators necessary for the implementation of guidelines. This process will also support stakeholders in developing adaptations and strategies for guideline implementation that are specifically tailored to the local context. This includes providing technical support to local guideline implementers in creating training manuals, flowcharts, and quality indicators, as well as participating in stakeholder meetings. The anticipated impact of the guideline on the organization of intrapartum care may necessitate a reorganization of care delivery and redistribution of healthcare resources. Effective implementation of the recommendations outlined in the guideline may require adjustments to existing systems, such as patient records and registers. Various strategies to address these barriers and facilitate implementation are detailed in Section 4 and Annex 4 of the document. The implementation and impact of these recommendations will be monitored at the health-service, regional, and country levels. The WHO publication Standards for improving quality of maternal and newborn care in health facilities provides prioritized input, output, and outcome measures that can be used to define quality-of-care criteria and indicators with locally agreed targets. In collaboration with the monitoring and evaluation teams of the WHO Departments of Reproductive Health and Research (RHR) and Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (MCA), data on the implementation of the recommendations at the country and regional levels will be collected and evaluated in the short to medium term to assess their impact on national policies of individual WHO Member States. Methods such as interrupted time series, clinical audits, or criterion-based audits may be employed to gather relevant data on the practices outlined in the guideline. The guideline will be updated systematically and continuously in accordance with the WHO process for updating maternal and perinatal health guidelines. An Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG) for maternal and perinatal health recommendations will convene annually to review WHO’s current portfolio of recommendations, prioritize new and existing questions for recommendation development, and update as needed. Recommendations included in this guideline will be regularly reviewed and prioritized by the Executive GSG. If new evidence emerges that could potentially impact the current evidence base for any of the recommendations, the recommendation will be updated. If no new reports or information are identified for a particular recommendation, it will be revalidated. The WHO Steering Group will continue to monitor research developments in the area of intrapartum care, particularly for questions where no evidence was found or where recommendations are supported by low-quality evidence. In such cases, new recommendations or changes to published recommendations may be warranted. Any concerns regarding the validity of a recommendation will be promptly communicated via the guideline’s website, and plans will be made to update the recommendation as needed.
